label: i-MO 310 4G bonding router
description: i-MO 310 - multi-channel bonding router for small branches and temporary or mobile sites: 6x Gigabit Ethernet ports individually configurable as WAN or LAN, a single 12 V supply (upgradable to 10-30 V DC), up to 128 GB internal flash with an optional NAS module, one USB 2.0 port, an RS232 serial console and a 2.4 GHz 802.11 b/g/n access point. Up to 3 internal LTE/UMTS module slots and 6 SIMs are options, not part of the base unit.
notes: Read the port row exactly as written: '**LAN / WAN Interface - 6 Gigabit Ethernet ports that individually configurable for WAN or LAN function. LAN ports can be bridged together to act as a switch.**' That is a *configurable* six, not a 1-WAN-5-LAN split, and this catalogue carries one role per port - so all six are declared `lan` in one bridge group, which is the factory state the second sentence describes, and this note carries the fact that any of them can be reassigned to WAN. A spec file that picked a split would be inventing which two ports the customer's two bonded WANs land on. **No cellular ports.** The base appliance has *slots*: 'Embedded Modems - 3 x internal slots for LTE/UMTS modules', 'Cellular Data SIMS - 6'. Nothing is fitted as standard and the option is not a port, so the wwan side is absent - use the kit SKUs where a modem is included. Same reasoning as the components clause in `docs/DEVICE_REGISTRY.md`. **The radio is 2.4 GHz only:** 'WiFi WLAN Access Point - 802.11 b/g/n', 2.412-2.472 GHz, 17 dBm. The page quotes no PHY rate, so `300M` is the 802.11n 2x2 ceiling this catalogue uses for a single-stream-class radio and not a figure from the datasheet. Console is the '**Management Port - RS232 serial console**' row; it carries no connector field, because a console port is not an Ethernet socket however its cable ends. 5x SMA are antenna connectors, not network interfaces.
